key_insight: Neural Operator Splitting learns physically interpretable fractional steps instead of full-step fluid evolution, reducing rollout error in complex geometries.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate repeated fluid simulations across varying geometries while retaining the structure of fractional-step numerical schemes.
method: Train separate neural operators on intermediate states from a numerical solver.
Use conditional-linear Fourier neural operators to preserve linear state mappings while conditioning nonlinearly on inputs such as geometry.
Apply symmetry sampling and corrective cycling to limit autoregressive error accumulation.
evidence_signal: In 2D and 3D flow experiments, the full model reduced mean relative L2 rollout error by 68% and 40%, respectively, versus a single full-step neural operator; inference was approximately 1,000× faster per step than the Monte Carlo solver at comparable error.
watch_item: Training requires solver-generated intermediate states, and the abstract does not establish generalization beyond the tested geometries and flow conditions.
paper_title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
